# Graham Priest — *One* (2014)

## Bibliographic identity

The selected object is Graham Priest, *One: Being an Investigation into the Unity of Reality and of Its Parts, Including the Singular Object which is Nothingness* (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2014). Metadata verified against the OUP catalogue and review records. The book has not yet been acquired; all quotations below are transcribed from published reviews — Jason Turner's NDPR review and McIntosh's review are the principal carriers — and every card requires collation against the printed pages before promotion to quotation-ready.

## Chicago 18 forms

**Shortened note:** Priest, *One*.

**Bibliography:** Priest, Graham. *One: Being an Investigation into the Unity of Reality and of Its Parts, Including the Singular Object which is Nothingness*. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2014.

## Source scholarship

The book's problem is ancient: what makes a partite object one thing rather than a mere plurality of its parts? Any answer that posits a unifying ingredient invites Bradley's regress — if the unifier is one more thing among the parts, something must unify *it* with them, and so on without end. Priest's answer is the gluon, "the unifier of a partite object," and his escape from the regress is deliberately contradictory: the gluon is identical to each of the parts while being none of them — an object both one and many. In Turner's transcription of the first-person formulation: "There is something that I am identical to and that each of my parts is also identical to" (p. 60, via NDPR). The regress then never starts, because, as McIntosh's review carries it, "the question of what unifies a, b, c and g is moot if each of a, b, and c is identical to g" — there is no residual gap between unifier and unified for a further relation to bridge. The price is a non-transitive, dialetheically tolerant identity: the gluon is identical to each part without the parts being thereby identical to one another.

From this local machinery the book scales up. Because every object has its unity through a gluon, and gluons bind objects into wider structures of dependence, Priest argues that "all things are one" (p. 55); and the account of being is openly relational: "For something to be one thing is for it to have its being by relating to other things" (p. 202). A third of the book works Buddhist material directly — emptiness, Indra's net, nothingness — and the convergence is stated in Priest's own compression: "to be is to be one, and to be one is to be empty." The limit case is nothingness itself, treated not as absence of subject matter but as a singular object: nothingness "is the fusion of the empty set, and is its own gluon" — the self-unifying zero-case where the machinery closes on itself.

## Essay use

### Source's relevant contribution

Gluon theory as a rigorous Western formalization of the one-and-many problem that ends, by its own argument, in relational being, emptiness, and a self-unifying nothing — the nearest formal neighbour to the essay's mono-poly structure.

### Licensed essay use

- Chain *One* into the Mono-Poly argument nodes ([[Mono-Poly: Whole and Many]], [[A12-Mono-Poly-One-All-Whole-Many|Mono-Poly]]) and [[46-s50-p3-4-2-mono-poly]] as a Western formal neighbour: an analytically worked case in which unity-of-the-many demands a contradictory unifier and being turns out relational.
- Use the nothingness-as-own-gluon limit case beside the essay's ground #0 as a structural echo, explicitly marked as echo.
- Use the book's Buddhist third (emptiness, Indra's net) to connect this house to [[symbolon/episteme/sources/indian-philosophy/dushun/dushun-cleary-2000-jewel-net-indra/dushun-cleary-2000-jewel-net-indra.md|dushun-cleary-2000-jewel-net-indra]] and the Huayan strand.

### Claim boundary

The essay chains *One* as neighbour, not as validation: QL's mono-poly structure is not derived from gluon theory, and Priest's conclusions do not confirm QL's. The reception gates apply — Turner (NDPR) argues gluon theory needs a thicker notion of identity than dialetheism licenses; McIntosh itemizes the price of admission as dialetheism, paraconsistency, non-transitive identity, noneism, and impossible worlds. The essay must cite the neighbour with its costs attached, and the identification of Priest's nothingness with QL's #0 is the essay's own Offered move.
